title: A 2.0.0 CLI refuses a workspace this release applied a generated set to, until `ia host claude --remove --apply` is run with this release
summary: The projection ownership state keeps its format name, ia.host-projection-state.v1, and now lists the generated agent and skill files beside the packet's, and .claude/settings.local.json holds one IA hook group per authored `@hook`, owned through .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json. A published 2.0.0 @inventarch/cli or @inventarch/distribution on such a workspace: every `ia host claude` plan, apply or removal, `ia project claude` and the install refresh first look for IA guard groups, recognize each hook group by its launcher's guard arguments, find no 2.0.0 guard ownership state for it, and refuse with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION ("An IA guard group has no matching ownership state; remove only that guard group before retiring steward files"), which asks the user to delete IA's own group by hand; a state that lists a generated skill (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is refused as an invalid projection ownership state (IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID), for codex too; a claude state that lists generated agents and no skill reads each agent as a 1.x steward file and deletes it as legacy; and while a hook registration is interrupted, guard-pending.json holds format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1, so 2.0.0 refuses host writes with IA-DIST-RECOVERY-REQUIRED and its `ia recover guard` refuses the journal as an unknown guard recovery format. The state format name is kept rather than bumped: a new name would make 2.0.0 refuse every workspace this release applied, those it can still read (a state with the packet's files only) included, and the hook groups, which that state does not hold, would refuse the same way. To hand a workspace back to a 2.0.0 CLI, first run `ia host claude --remove --apply` with this release (and `ia host codex --remove --apply` where codex is registered), which removes the hook groups, their ownership state, the generated files and the receipt, then run 2.0.0's `ia host <claude|codex> --apply`. A workspace that authors no `@agent-profile`, `@playbook` or `@hook` gets nothing new written and stays readable by 2.0.0.
